rv.q: Admittedly Anne-Marie Duff is not obvious casting as the happily hedonistic Alma. But she invests the role with a fragile intensity as if she is experiencing a bad dream, and has one wonderful moment when her eyes gaze adoringly at her young son who has been strategically placed in the courtroom.
After Sharrock’s rapturous rediscovery of Rattigan’s After the Dance last year, this is merely routine.
